name: Aniruddha
role: Grandson of Krishna, husband of Princess Usha
summary: Aniruddha is the son of Pradyumna and the grandson of Krishna and Rukmini. His name means unconquerable, and his love story with Princess Usha is retold in Assam, Gujarat, Andhra and beyond.
about: In the Bhagavata Purana and Harivamsa, Aniruddha is the son of Pradyumna and Rukmavati, and so the grandson of Krishna and Rukmini. Vaishnava tradition counts him among the four vyuha forms. The Bhagavata Purana tells that Princess Usha, daughter of the asura king Banasura, dreams of him and her friend Chitralekha uses her art and yogic power to bring him to Usha. Banasura holds Aniruddha captive, which leads to a war between the Yadavas and Banasura's side, with Shiva as the protector of Banasura. The Bhagavata Purana says Krishna's side prevails, while the Agnigarh tradition in Tezpur says Brahma stopped the war and Shiva and Krishna settled it by talking. The couple are married in Dvaraka. Their son Vajra later becomes king of Indraprastha. Tezpur in Assam links the story to its old name Sonitpur, and different regions tell the tale with their own details.
kidSummary: Aniruddha is Krishna's grandson in the Hindu stories. His name means unconquerable. In the best-known tale, a princess named Usha dreams about him and her clever friend Chitralekha brings him to her. After a great battle, the two are married, and the city of Tezpur in Assam still remembers the legend.

story.title: A dream of a prince
story.text: Princess Usha of the Bana kingdom dreams of a young man she has never met. When she wakes, she tells her friend Chitralekha about it.

story.title: Chitralekha the painter
story.text: Chitralekha draws pictures of many princes until Usha points to the one from her dream. He is Aniruddha, grandson of Krishna.

story.title: A secret journey
story.text: In the Bhagavata Purana, Chitralekha uses her yogic powers to bring Aniruddha from Dvaraka to Usha's rooms. The two get to know each other and lose track of the days.

story.title: The great battle
story.text: Usha's father Banasura holds Aniruddha captive, and after Narada brings the news, the Yadavas march to his city. In the Bhagavata Purana Shiva stands beside Banasura and Krishna's side prevails; Tezpur tells it differently, with Brahma stepping in.

story.title: A wedding in Dvaraka
story.text: Banasura gives his blessing, and Usha and Aniruddha are married. They go to Dvaraka, where their son Vajra is later born.

teaches: Friends can help carry love and courage
A war ends when people choose to listen
Pride can be softened with patience
emblems: Boar aspect in Vaishnava vyuha images

facts.text: Her friend Chitralekha, a skilled artist, sketched portraits of the Vrishni princes until Usha recognised the face from her dream.
In the Bhagavata Purana, Chitralekha used yogic powers to shrink Aniruddha to the size of a doll and carry him out of Krishna's palace.
In the Bhagavata Purana, Shiva's fever Jvara, shown with three heads and three feet, is overcome by the cold fever sent by Krishna.
In the Bhagavata Purana, Krishna spared Banasura because Vishnu had once promised Bali never to harm his family, but he cut Banasura's thousand arms down to four.
In Vaishnava iconography Aniruddha is linked with the boar form Varaha, linked with ferocity and sovereignty. In the Vaikuntha Chaturmurti a boar head projects from the side of Vishnu's head.
A hillock called Agnigarh in Tezpur, Assam, is said to be where Banasura kept Usha in a fortress ringed by fire, and the name joins agni (fire) with garh (fort).
The Bengali Manasamangala poems say Usha and Aniruddha were reborn as Behula and Lakshmindara and married again.
Banasura burst into Usha's rooms and found her playing dice with Aniruddha, tiny as a doll, then bound him with the magic ropes of Varuna.
Tezpur's own tradition says Brahma asked Krishna and Shiva to stop the war and stood between them. Krishna then persuaded Shiva that Banasura was in the wrong, and Banasura agreed to the wedding.
Banasura boasted to Shiva that, with his thousand arms, even elephants feared him. Shiva answered that his banner would fall when his pride met its match in battle.

At Aniruddha's wedding to Rochana, Rukmi cheated Balarama at dice and insulted the Yadavas, and Balarama killed him. Rukmi was Aniruddha's own maternal grandfather, since his mother Rukmavati was Rukmi's daughter.
In the Mahabharata's aftermath, after the Yadava brawl left Aniruddha's son Vajra as the only surviving prince, Arjuna led the survivors to Indraprastha and crowned Vajra king.

The Yadava siege of Banasura's city used 12 akshauhinis. One akshauhini is 218,700 units (chariots, elephants, horses and foot soldiers), so the army was about 2.6 million, more than the Pandavas' seven at Kurukshetra.
Aniruddha had a second son named Mrigaketana with his first wife Rochana, while his elder son Vajra was born to Usha.
An 18th-century Gujarati poem, Okhaharan by Premanand Bhatt, retells the story with Usha called Okha, and Vedam Venkataraya Sastry's Telugu play Usha Parinayam of 1901 tells it too.
In the Bhagavata Purana duel, each weapon met its match: a brahma weapon against a brahma weapon, a mountain weapon against wind, rain against fire, and Narayana's weapon against Shiva's Pashupata.
When Banasura attacked Krishna, the Bhagavata Purana says Krishna blew his conch and the sound alone killed Banasura's charioteer and shattered his chariot.
Aniruddha was held captive for a month, until the sage Narada told the Yadavas in Dvaraka where he was.
Chitralekha's name means artist in Sanskrit, and it was her drawn portraits of the Vrishni princes that let Usha name the man from her dream.
Some traditions call Aniruddha a jana avatar of Vishnu because he was so like his grandfather Krishna, and he is counted among the four Vrishni heroes of the chatur-vyuha.

quiz.q: What does the name Aniruddha mean?
Who found Aniruddha for Princess Usha?
quiz.why: Chitralekha, an artist with yogic powers, found him and brought him to Usha.

quiz.q: Which city in Assam is linked to the Usha and Aniruddha legend?
quiz.why: Tezpur, once called Sonitpur, has Agnigarh hill linked to the story.
He is the son of Pradyumna and Rukmavati.

quiz.q: How many arms did Banasura have before Krishna reduced them?
quiz.why: Banasura had a thousand arms thanks to a boon from Shiva.
